Sampled HR@10 can conceal poor catalog ranking and reverse model comparisons, even in expectation. Krichene–Rendle establish this inconsistency; sequential-recommendation experiments find that both uniform and popularity sampling can disagree with full-catalog rankings. RecSys 2025 research further examines sampling reliability under varying exposure bias: changing the negative sampler does not automatically recover preference quality. [Sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [sequential-model study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045), [2025 reliability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398).

Finite-population calibration follows directly: let N be eligible negative items and K the number preceding the target under the evaluator’s tie rule. With 99 uniformly sampled unique negatives, X ~ Hypergeometric(N,K,99), and P(sampled hit@10)=P(X≤9); catalog hit@10 requires K≤9. Thus sampled success can coexist with hundreds of catalog outrankers. This derivation requires uniform sampling without replacement; popularity-weighted or hard-negative sampling needs its own sampling law. One sampled hit cannot identify catalog rank. [NIST distribution definition](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/ch8/hypcdf.pdf), [2024 finite-population confidence bounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.06722).

Recommended diagnostic application: freeze training prefixes and each category’s single NextItNet; score eligible catalog items in chunks for a bounded user subset, counting outrankers exactly. Compare repeated independent 99-negative draws against hypergeometric predictions; report draw variability separately from user-bootstrap uncertainty. Define popularity strata using training-prefix counts only, then audit target strata and hard-negative stress sets separately. These are diagnostic proposals, not measured results. Preserve the pinned seed-42, 200-user/category macro validation HR@10 as the selection metric; label catalog, repeated-draw, and stratified results separately.
